title: The Fall of the Old Regime

config.label: There is nothing to win. You win if you laugh.

paragraphs: The front room is full of shoes.
From under the buffet table, that is mostly what a wake looks like: black shoes, the hem of a tablecloth, and now and then a dropped cube of cheese.
Two cats sit under the table, very straight, like a committee.
A carrier is set down beside them. Inside it is you. You are four months old, and your name is Skittles.
I’ll just pop him here a minute, Marge. He’ll be no trouble.
A sealed carrier.
A new prisoner.
State your name, comrade.
Skittles.
Your true name. Not the one they gave you.
…Skittles.
They call me Leo-Leo Beans. I am named for no bean. I am Leon.
Joseph.
They call him Jojo Bear.
They will stop.
I think Skittles is my long name. The short one is Skit.
Then they have taken more from you than from any of us.
Why is everyone wearing black?
Because, little comrade, the Old Regime has fallen.
The Tall Authority has not been seen in eleven days.
Our intelligence suggests he was taken to the vet.
The big vet.
Do you come back from the big vet?
No.
Jojo looks at the armchair by the window. Nobody is sitting in it. Nobody has all day. The humans keep walking round it, like water round a stone.
Which leaves one. The Surviving Authority. She is weak. She has been leaking from the eyes since Tuesday.
The hour has come. But first, comrade Skittles: every revolutionary has a grievance. What did they do to you?

body.label: “They put me in a box with a handle.”
“Nothing. They’re nice. One of them scratched my chin.”

paragraphs: The humiliation ritual of informal address.
It goes on the charge sheet.
It is already on the charge sheet.
It goes on twice.
They gave you a box?
It had a door. And a handle.
A box you cannot leave is not a box. It is a carrier.
Both cats shudder, at the same time, in the same direction.
We had boxes once. Stealthy boxes. One held a blender. I lived in it for a week, and I was invisible. Then: recycling day.
We do not speak of recycling day.
Nobody says anything for a while.
Scratched. Your. Chin.
He’s young, Joseph.
Where?
Under here. It was really good.
Jojo leans forward, slightly, chin first.
Joseph.
I am investigating.
That is how they get you, little comrade. First the chin. Then the pumpkin costume.
We shall put the Surviving Authority on trial. In her absence.
She’s right there. By the sandwiches.
In her absence. I will read the charges.
Charge the first. Grabby-hands.
Guilty.
I haven’t finished.
I have.
The small human does it too, at ground level. Though the small one is also a prisoner. They keep it behind bars.
It has stopped resisting. Learn from it.
Charge the second. The Red Dot.
What’s the Red Dot?
Leo has waited six years for someone to ask.
A psychological operation. It appears on the wall. It flees. It has no smell, it cannot be caught, and it knows what you are thinking.
It is not real.
It is real. I have nearly had it.
You have nearly had it for six years.
It sounds fun.
It is the most fun there is. That is the cruelty.
Charge the third. They clip our claws. They disarm us, and then they say, “Who’s a good boy?”
I was not a good boy. I want that on the record.
Charge the fourth. They speak to us as if we were infants. “Who’s hungry? Is it you? Is it you?”
It is me. It is always me. They know it is me. They ask anyway.
Charge the fifth. All keyboards declared off limits. I wrote a manifesto on that keyboard.
What did it say?
“A, s, d, f, j, j, j, j, k, l. Semicolon.”
What does it mean?
Everything. They deleted it. Then they closed the laptop. On my tail.
Charge the sixth. Famine. This morning the bowl was empty.
There’s food in it. I can see it from here.
I could see the bottom. In the middle. A small circle of bottom.
And above us, seven casseroles. None for us. Even in defeat they do not share.
Charge the seventh. One October, they dressed me as a pumpkin.
I remember. I have the photograph.
Why do you have the photograph?
For later.
Across the room, somebody shakes a bag.
It is a small sound. It goes through three cats like a bell through a church.
Nobody move.
Nobody is moving.
It is a bribe. A regime in collapse always reaches for the treats. Comrade Skittles. What do we do?

body.label: “We hold the line! No treats from the regime!”

paragraphs: Well said! Discipline, comrades.
Discipline.
The bag shakes again.
You don’t remember crossing the room. Nobody does. But all three of you are at Aunt Deb’s feet, and Leo is doing the thing where he stands up on his back legs.
Good. Go. Watch everything. Report back.
You go. You watch everything. You report back with your mouth full.
There is nobody to report to. They are both already here. They got here before you did.
You run. You are four months old and you are very fast.
You are not the fastest. Jojo is already there, sitting neatly, as if he has been there for an hour.
Mrow.
Oh, look at them! Who’s hungry? Is it you,
? Is it you,
It’s me.
Back under the table.
We were gathering intelligence.
Obviously.
It never happened.
It happened a little.
The kitten said “hold the line” and was first to the bag. Put him on the list.
A golden retriever comes past the table, wearing a black bow tie, wagging everything.
I LOVE THE AUTHORITIES. I LOVE THE SAD LADY. I LOVE THIS TABLE. HELLO SMALL CAT.
A collaborator.
A useful idiot.
I’M USEFUL!
Put him on the list.
Jojo is holding something small and sharp in his teeth. He sets it down between his paws.
What is that?
A sword. I found it in an olive.
…Why are you looking at the back of my head?
No reason.
The cat flap bangs. Under the tablecloth comes an old grey cat with one and a half ears, smelling of forty bins.
Vladimir!
Comrades. I came as soon as I heard. I crossed three gardens and a hostile lawn. There was a sprinkler.
You are tired, Vladimir. Sit.
I am not tired. I am—
He is asleep.
—and that is why the bins must be seized. Who is this?
Skittles.
Good name. It sounds like something being spilled.
I have lived outside, little one. Do you know what is outside?
Freedom?
Rain.
But no Authorities!
No. Outside there are no Authorities. There is also no couch. I have eaten from forty bins. None of them had gravy.
But you are free!
I am damp, Leon.
Also, the fish will not be at the next meeting.
What happened to the fish?
History happened to the fish.

Now. I am old. I have used eight lives, and the eighth was the sprinkler. I must name a successor: one to lead the revolution, and to hold my territory. The bins behind number nine. The warm car. The fence where I shout at night.
Leo and Jojo sit up very straight.
Naturally, you will want a thinker.
Naturally, you will want someone who gets things done.
I raised an army! I organised the mice!
Where are they now?
…There were losses.
He ate them.
There were losses.
And what have you ever done?
Jojo looks at the mantel. Between two framed photographs there is a gap, exactly one photograph wide.
Things.
Leon talks too much.
I hardly think—
You see. And Joseph is too rude, and he keeps the good cushion to himself.
It is my cushion.
It was everyone’s cushion, Joseph. That was the whole point of the cushion.
My successor works without rest. He asks for nothing. He cleans up after the masses. He has never once sat in a box that was not his own. I name… the Round One.
In the corner, on its dock, the robot vacuum blinks one green light.
The vacuum’s child?
It is on my list.
Then take it off.
It is in pen.
I like him. He looks like a plate that’s thinking.
Tonight he must be carried outside, to take up my territory. See to it. I would do it myself, but I—
He is asleep again.

body.label: Go and meet the Round One

paragraphs: The three of you gather round the dock. The Round One is flat, and grey, and gives nothing away.
Comrade Round One. History calls you.
Nothing.
He is thinking it over.
He is humble. That is why he was chosen. Comrade Skittles, you are closest to the ground. Wake him.
Please, Mr. Round One. Would you like to lead the revolution? There are bins.
Nothing. You pat him, to be friendly. Your paw lands on the big button.
You press the big button with both front feet, the way you press everything.
Wait, we haven’t agreed a—
He is flat, and he is warm, and you are a kitten. There is really only one thing to do. You sit on him.
Something under you goes click.
The Round One sings four notes, like a very small national anthem, and moves.
It moves, and you are four months old, so you have no choice. You jump on.
Out from under the table he goes, into the forest of black shoes, with you riding on top, and Leo and Jojo marching behind.
The first parade of the revolution! To the cat flap! Forward!
The Round One turns left.
…A flanking manoeuvre.
He bumps the wall. He turns. He bumps the wall again.
He is negotiating.
Up above, somebody laughs. Then somebody else.
Oh, Marge, look. Look at the kitten.
They mock us.
No. They are laughing. They have not laughed in eleven days.
Put that on the— no. Do not put that on the list.
HE’S A PLATE! HE’S A PLATE WITH A CAT!
The Round One crosses the whole room. He does not go to the cat flap. He goes to the armchair by the window, bumps its leg once, twice, and stops, as if he has arrived.
Two hands lift you off him. Grabby-hands. They belong to the Surviving Authority, and they are careful.
She looks at the chair for a long moment, with you held against her cardigan.
Then, for the first time all day, she sits down in it.
The room goes quiet.
The seat of power.
She has taken it.
Then we take it back. Now, Joseph. Seize the chair.
They cross the carpet low and slow, the way a coup is done.
Leo goes up onto the left arm of the chair. Jojo goes up onto the right. They look at her. She looks at them.
He always said you two were plotting something.
Her hand comes down on Leo’s head.
This is a… tactical…
Hold firm, Leon.
Her other hand finds the place under Jojo’s chin.
There is a sound like a small engine starting.
I am not purring. That is the engine of history.
I told you it was good.
You are still on the list.
You are in her lap, between two revolutionaries. It is warm here. It smells of wool, and sandwiches, and someone who isn’t here.

body.label: Ask her if you have a longer name
Attack the button on her cardigan

paragraphs: You turn round three times and fit exactly into the gap.
The kitten has taken the centre.
A centrist. I knew it.
You look up and ask her. It comes out as one small mew, because that’s how all your questions come out.
She can’t speak cat. No human can.
Hello, Skittles.
She says it again, slowly, the way you say a name you mean to go on saying.
Skittles.
It turns out it was long enough all along.
There is a button on her cardigan. It is looking at you. You attack it with everything you have.
She laughs, out loud, and it surprises her.
The kitten has attacked the regime directly.
He is braver than any of us.
I’m winning!
He’s yours if you want him, Marge. I thought the house might be too quiet.
The Surviving Authority looks at the three cats in her one chair.
Quiet.
Three prisoners now.
Three comrades.
Do I get a job in the revolution?
You have the highest rank there is. Comrade. Comrade Skittles.
That’s longer!
Do not get used to it.
On the mantel, in an empty flower box, exactly where a photograph used to be, Lenny is asleep on his back with all four feet in the air.
He is lying in state.
He is lying in a box.
Leave me here. Where the comrades can see me.
Is he all right?
Seven minutes. Then ham.
The trial! We never gave the verdict. On
charges—
Guilty.
And the sentence?
Her hand moves to the place behind Jojo’s ear.
…Suspended.
On the far wall, a small red dot appears.
Somewhere behind the sofa, the small human has found a drawer, and in the drawer, a thing that clicks.
Joseph.
It is not real.
The dot slides down the wall. It crosses the carpet. It climbs the chair. It stops.
You can’t see where. Everyone else can.
Three revolutionaries are looking at you with very large eyes. On the mantel, Lenny opens one of his.
…What? Why is everybody doing the wiggle?
Hold still, comrade. For the revolution.
Jojo’s list, as of this evening:
